tools.name: animation_analyze
tools.description: Analyze one animation clip at 60 FPS and render graph-space picture evidence. Pass a clips array containing exactly one scene character and one loaded Clip name or Assets/Packages Clip path. The result contains one clip analysis and one pictures evidence object; temporal positions use absolute Timeline-global 60 FPS frames. External Clips are appended to the character's Kimodo Timeline and never modified.

documentation.when_to_use: Analyze one loaded animation Clip and produce structured motion data with renderable image evidence.
behavior: Use the scene character and a loaded Clip name or an Assets/Packages asset path.
Open returned pictures before making visual claims; use structured fields for measurements and temporal positions.
result_notes: Returns one clip analysis and one pictures object; analysis frame positions use Timeline-global 60 FPS coordinates.
scene_effects: An external Clip asset is appended to the character's Kimodo Timeline for analysis; the source asset is not modified.
limits: The clips array must contain exactly one Clip.
Static pictures do not establish playback continuity, velocity smoothness, foot sliding, or other time-continuous properties.

picture.description: Unified graph-space picture request with tiles and output mode.

resolution.description: Final picture tile resolution in pixels; accepts 64 through 4096. Rendering uses a 2x supersample and downsamples to this size. Defaults to 1920.

tools.name: analysis.video
tools.description: Estimate a per-frame SMPL-X pose sequence from a local video. This starts an asynchronous analysis job; poll kimodo_get_generation with its request_id. The result includes raw SMPL-X poses and matching FullBody constraints in the existing raw constraint format; it does not create or apply a Unity animation.

documentation.when_to_use: Use when a video file should be converted into a time-ordered SMPL-X pose array for downstream retargeting or analysis.
behavior: Pass an absolute video_path that the QuickServer machine can read. Supported formats are MP4, MOV, M4V, AVI, and MKV; the file must not exceed 2 GiB.

The command returns immediately with status=accepted and a request_id. Poll kimodo_get_generation using that exact id until status is completed, failed, or canceled; do not submit the video again just to check progress.
For a two-person video, optionally set person to left or right to select the performer by screen position. Omit person for the default selection.
result_notes: A completed request returns poses in source-video order plus one top-level constraints array, fps, frame_count, source_frame_count, joint_names, betas, and rest_joints_m.

Each pose contains raw global_orient_axis_angle, body_pose_axis_angle, and translation_m values. The top-level constraints array uses the same merged raw FullBody constraint format accepted by animation generation.

Rotations are axis-angle radians; translation and rest joints are in meters. The global coordinate space is gravity-aligned Y-up. Optional incam_* fields use OpenCV camera coordinates: X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.
The result does not create a clip, Playable track, character binding, or timeline edit.
scene_effects: Read-only; does not create, modify, or clear Unity scene objects or animation assets.
limits: The top-level constraints array groups the whole sequence into the existing raw FullBody payload; the command still does not return a rendered animation or create a Unity Humanoid muscle track.
The request can fail if QuickServer's GVHMR runtime, checkpoints, or the SMPL-X Avatar asset are unavailable.

video_path.description: Absolute path to a local video readable by QuickServer.

person.description: Select one performer by screen side in a two-person video.

examples.description: Estimate SMPL-X poses from a video, then poll for the pose array.

tools.name: analysis.picture
tools.description: Estimate one SMPL-X pose from a local still image. This starts an asynchronous analysis job; poll kimodo_get_generation with its request_id. The result includes raw SMPL-X pose data and a FullBody constraint in the existing raw constraint format; it does not create or apply a Unity animation.

documentation.when_to_use: Use when a still image should be converted into a single SMPL-X pose sample for downstream retargeting or analysis.
behavior: Pass an absolute image_path for a PNG, JPG, or JPEG file that the QuickServer machine can read. The file must not exceed 2 GiB.

The command returns immediately with status=accepted and a request_id. Poll kimodo_get_generation using that exact id until status is completed, failed, or canceled; do not submit the image again just to check progress.
The estimator temporarily treats the still image as a one-second clip and returns one pose sample from it.
result_notes: A completed request returns one raw SMPL-X pose plus a top-level constraints array containing the matching raw FullBody constraint, along with joint_names, betas, and rest_joints_m.
The pose contains raw global_orient_axis_angle, body_pose_axis_angle, and translation_m values. The constraints array uses the same format accepted by animation generation.

Rotations are axis-angle radians; translation and rest joints are in meters. The global coordinate space is gravity-aligned Y-up. Optional incam_* fields use OpenCV camera coordinates: X-right, Y-down, Z-forward.
The result does not create a clip, Playable track, character binding, or timeline edit.
scene_effects: Read-only; does not create, modify, or clear Unity scene objects or animation assets.
limits: The constraints array is a raw FullBody payload with one frame; the command still does not return a rendered animation or create a Unity Humanoid muscle track.
The request can fail if QuickServer's GVHMR runtime, checkpoints, or the SMPL-X Avatar asset are unavailable.

tools.name: kimodo_generate_animation
tools.description: Start asynchronous generation for a character in the current scene context. Command-created Timeline Clips enable AutoBegin anchoring automatically; explicit first-frame or In/Out samples take precedence. The accepted response contains request_id, status, and non-blocking request/constraint warnings; pose/effect safety preflight runs only when the same point constraint explicitly contains both pose and effect, never for effect-only constraints. These warnings are not measured joint positions in the generated motion; use pose_get then pose_test to measure sampled joint positions and contact reach after generation. Supply trajectory settings only when the requested path is known from explicit requirements or confirmed scene/analysis evidence; prompt wording never selects path options.

documentation.when_to_use: Submit one animation generation request for a character in the current scene context.
behavior: Describe one simple semantic action in prompt; aim for 25 words or fewer.
Represent exact body pose, root position, effector targets, duration, path, loop, and Clip windows in their explicit fields when required.
Save request_id and use kimodo_get_generation to poll; do not resubmit a running request.
result_notes: The accepted response contains request_id, status, non-blocking check results, and warnings. Pose/effect safety preflight runs only when the same point constraint explicitly contains both pose and effect; effect-only constraints skip it.
On completion, kimodo_get_generation returns the generated Clip metadata, asset path, animation_id, and available generation diagnostics.
scene_effects: A completed result is appended as a Timeline Clip; existing completed Clips are retained.
The first scene pose is used as the automatic starting anchor unless explicit first-frame or In/Out samples take precedence.
limits: Trajectory overrides require an explicit requirement or confirmed scene/analysis evidence; prompt words do not select path options.
analysis_option is lightweight generation-time analysis, not the full animation_analyze command.
Command checks validate supported request boundaries; they do not judge semantic or artistic quality.

character.description: Scene character name or object_ref. Session preview objects are rejected; use the source scene character.

prompt.description: Short semantic description of the current Clip's action; aim for 25 words or fewer. Express exact FullBody, position, and effector anchors through structured constraints.

duration_frames.description: Duration in 60 FPS frames; defaults to 300 frames (5 seconds).

loop.description: Enable loop preprocessing, or provide per-axis endpoint locks with {enabled, lock_pos:{x,y,z}, lock_rot:{x,y,z}}.

enabled.description: Enable bounded loop preprocessing; defaults to true when the loop object is supplied.

path.description: Optional Root2D path override. Use only when the trajectory is known from an explicit requirement or confirmed scene/analysis evidence; never infer these fields from prompt keywords. Any angle enables path override; distance replaces the measured path length; heading is applied after path composition.

generation.description: Optional model and deterministic generation settings.

analysis_option.description: Optional generation-time lightweight analysis. When enabled, generation returns sparse salient keyframe markers and foot-contact changes; it does not run the full animation_analyze command.

constraints.description: Point constraints are selected by optional pose, root2d, and effect data; multiple fields at one frame compose by channel. Pose/effect safety preflight runs only when the same point constraint explicitly contains both pose and effect; effect-only constraints skip it. root_path and inout remain separate constraint forms; duplicate frames are rejected; command frames use 60 FPS.

pose.description: External Pose slot in the current scene context.

root2d.description: Planar root position and heading constraint; supply both channels together.

frame.description: First path frame; defaults to the clip start. Use a confirmed path for the intended character and motion; root_path generates only start and end Root2D constraints, not intermediate route enforcement.

path.description: Confirmed analyzed Root Path slot for the intended character and motion, returned by animation_analyze at clip.root_trajectory.path.

mode.description: Outside pads generation with source context then crops it off; inside constrains the returned clip's start/end windows. Output duration is preserved.

clip.description: Safe completed source Clip name in the current scene context.

character.description: Defaults to the generation character; cross-character sources are not supported.

frame.description: Optional boundary frame at 60 FPS, local to the Clip's played Timeline range. Defaults: outside In=last model frame / Out=first; inside In=first / Out=last.

window_frames.description: Coverage at 60 FPS. Converted to model frames by ceil(window_frames * model_fps / 60), minimum 1; never silently shortened.

sample_count.description: Distinct samples within the converted window. One preserves the seam; multiple samples include both endpoints.

tools.name: pose_get
tools.description: Sample one absolute Timeline-global frame at 60 FPS, or select mode scene_pose / skeleton_rest_pose to read the original scene Animator or Avatar rest pose. Every response includes character_root, the bound scene GameObject root Transform in world space; data.root is the sampled Pose root channel. Every call creates an External Pose slot and returns {track,index}.

documentation.when_to_use: Materialize an External Pose from a Timeline frame, the current scene Animator pose, or the Avatar skeleton rest pose.
behavior: For an animation frame, pass its absolute Timeline-global frame at 60 FPS.
Inspect the returned Pose and confirm its role before using its {track,index} reference as a generation constraint.
result_notes: Returns an External Pose reference, source details, character_root world Transform, and sampled Pose data.
character_root is the bound scene GameObject root; data.root is the sampled Pose root channel.
scene_effects: Every call creates an External Pose slot in the current scene context.
limits: A Timeline frame and scene_pose/skeleton_rest_pose mode are alternative source forms.
Use full_data only when all muscle and TQ channels are needed.

source.description: Select exactly one source form: a Timeline-global frame, the current scene Animator pose, or the Avatar skeleton rest pose.

character.description: Current scene character name or object_ref.

mode.description: Sample the original scene Animator's currently evaluated pose, or the Avatar's stored skeleton rest pose.

timeline_frame_60.description: Absolute Timeline-global frame at 60 FPS. Use animation_analyze to find the selected Clip's start frame, then add the clip-local frame offset.

full_data.description: Return all 49 muscles and TQ channels; defaults to false.

Capture the Humanoid Avatar's stored skeleton rest pose.

tools.name: pose_test
tools.description: Measure actual Humanoid joint world positions after evaluating any External Pose, including a pose sampled from a generated effect-only result. Optionally compare selected joints with world-space target positions; this is an explicit pose measurement, separate from generation-time non-blocking warnings.

documentation.when_to_use: Measure the actual world-space positions of Humanoid joints in an External Pose, optionally checking them against expected contact targets.
behavior: Call pose_get for the desired scene or Timeline frame first, then pass its returned pose reference.
Use targets when a contact or reach criterion needs a numerical pass/fail check; target positions and tolerances are in meters in world space.
result_notes: Returns measured joint world positions, optional target distances and tolerance results, and an overall status.
This samples the evaluated Pose rig; it does not judge whether the pose looks natural or whether a generated Clip plays smoothly.
scene_effects: Read-only with respect to the scene, Timeline, Pose slot, and animation assets; evaluation uses a transient preview rig.
limits: pose_test explicitly measures the actual joints in any sampled Pose, including after effect-only generation. Generation-time pose/effect safety preflight is separate and runs only when the same constraint explicitly includes both pose and effect.
Requires a valid Humanoid character and a Pose reference from the current context.

pose.description: External Pose slot in the current scene context.

joints.description: Humanoid joints to measure. Defaults to hips, head, hands, and feet; joints named in targets are included automatically.

targets.description: Optional expected world-space joint positions and per-target tolerances in meters.
